category_summary: **Model launches dominated the week.** The official **[MISSINGNO](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-ca99e6ac2f71)** reveal — a token-efficient coding and agentic reasoning model, free for a limited time on **Nous Portal** and usable in **Hermes Agent** — was the batch's top performer (~90k views), effectively answering **@Teknium**'s earlier [stealth-model teaser](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-b3cb97660eba) and capping a build-up of anticipation. Sentiment was strongly positive, with members like **@rlaope** [hyping the drop](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-cd80957db355) and urging others to try it. **Community showcases** highlighted real deployments: **@rlaope** demonstrated **[DeepSeek 4.1 Flash](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-5250627b2d62)** serving at ~1000 TPS underpinning their **hermes-agent** and **deepseek-harness** setups, with a cost/performance angle. **Hermes Agent support** remains a community strength — **@Teknium** fielded practical questions on [connecting **Claude** subscriptions](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-b4a7dc4562ec), [unified sessions/profile behavior](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-1124ac999c44), and the [Slack bot + async subagent pattern](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-16812e30bedb), reflecting a hands-on, developer-forward culture. The **AI-gaming vision** was the engagement magnet: **@Teknium**'s musing about [reviving **EverQuest** with AI](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-0751d7fcff26) drew 600+ likes and 135 replies, spiraling into playful brainstorming ([Skyrim/EverQuest races](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-5cd9751e2708), [a cat race](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-d5c0e3f4ee16), [tagged-user cameos](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-bc6812e8f89c), plus an [EVE Online aside](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-c3b7e251d63e)). **Competitive positioning** surfaced in threads where **@Teknium** criticized [rival agent products over persistence and state loss](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-c6635ccef8b8) and [debated what counts as an 'agent,'](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-55b796fc75fa) reinforcing the ethos that agents should keep memory and identity; his [open-source stance comment](/?date=2026-10-11&category=social#item-e559bdc3907d) rounds out the section. Below the top tier, most posts are low-substance replies, emoji reactions, and thread banter with minimal standalone newsletter value.
